chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyād, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Bukayr ibn Aʿyan, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: concerning

A man stole, but he was not apprehended. Then he stole another time, and he was caught. Then the evidence came, and they testified against him for the first theft and the last theft. So he said: “His hand is cut off for the first theft, and his foot is not cut off for the last theft.” It was said: How is that? He said: “Because the witnesses all testified in one sitting to the first theft and the last theft before he was punished for the first theft. But if the witnesses testified against him for the first theft, then withheld until his hand was cut off, then testified against him for the last theft, his left foot would be cut off.”

key_terms.السَّرِقَةِ: theft, the offense under discussion in the legal ruling
key_terms.الشُّهُودَ: the witnesses whose testimony establishes the crime
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: the legal proof or evidentiary basis brought before judgment
key_terms.تُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ: his hand is cut off, the hadd punishment for the first theft
key_terms.رِجْلُهُ الْيُسْرَى: his left foot, the punishment applied for a subsequent theft under the stated condition
key_terms.مَقَامٍ وَاحِدٍ: a single sitting or occasion in which the testimony was delivered

ai.seo_question: If someone committed theft twice but both thefts were proven at the same time, is the hand and foot both cut off?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal ruling concerning repeated theft and the sequencing of testimony and punishment. It indicates that the legal consequence for a later theft depends on whether it is established only after the first hadd punishment has already been carried out.
